full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment dated 30-9-2014 passed by the learned District Judge, Khulna dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 2008 allowing the Auction held on 28-7-2005 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the opposite party decree-holder filed Miscellaneous Case No. 181 of 1997 for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 8,86,859.99 from the petitioner and opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 before the District Judge, Khulna. The said Miscellaneous Case was decreed on 29-11-2001. 

 3. Being aggrieved, the petitioner judgment debtor filed appeal before the High Court Division against the judgment and decree of the learned District Judge. In appeal this Court directed the petitioner to pay Taka 50,000 instantly to the decree-holder opposite party and the rest amount by equal installments within the time fixed by the court. The judgment debtor petitioner did not comply with the order of this Court. Resultantly, the decree-holder opposite party filed Money Execution Case No. 28 of 2003 for recovery of the decretal money. 

 4. In the said execution case the mortgaged property was placed on auction for three times but no bidder participated in the bid. Finally, the decree-holder opposite party filed an application before the executing court seeking permission to participate in auction and purchase the property against the claim of the decree-holder. The executing court allowed the application and pursuant to that the decree-holder opposite party took part in auction and purchased the property and a sale certificate to that effect was issued by the court in favour of the decree-holder on 15-1-2006 which was duly registered with the Sub-Registrar, Khulna and delivered possession of the property to the decree-holder and disposed of the sale execution case with full satisfaction by order dated 25-4-2006. The petitioner then filed Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 2008 under Order XXI, rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the sale on the allegations that the auction was held fraudulently by practicing fraud. Decree-holder opposite party contested the case by filing written objection. The court below upon contest hearing rejected the case by the impugned judgment and order dated 30-9-2013. 

 6. The opposite party decree-holder contested the Rule by filing a counter affidavit contending, inter alia, that the petitioner has mortgaged the property as security against loan to the decree-holder opposite party. They being failed to make repayment of the said loan the decree-holder filed Miscellaneous Case No. 181 of 1997 in the court of District Judge, Khulna which was decreed and the decree-holder put the said decree in execution by filing Execution Case No. 28 of 2003. 

 7. In the said execution case the property in question was placed on auction but no bidder found. Subsequently, the decree-holder opposite party purchased the property against their claim and the court duly issued sale certificate and delivered possession of the same. After purchase, the opposite party decree-holder published a tender notice for sale of the property inviting quotation from intending purchaser. In response to tender notice, opposite party No. 5 along with others participated in the said tender and among the bidders, offer of the opposite party No. 5 was found highest and the property was sold to the opposite party No. 5 by registered sale deed No. 3001 dated 22-12-2013. 

 9. It is also stated that the petitioner knowing fully well about execution proceedings and purchase of the mortgaged property by the decree-holder, after a long time filed miscellaneous case challenging the auction only to harass and deprive the bona fide purchaser-opposite-party No. 1. It is also contended that the miscellaneous case filed under Order XXI, rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure is hopelessly time barred under Article 166 of the Limitation Act, as the case has not been filed within 30 (thirty) days from the date of auction as alleged. 

 10. Mr. Ahmed Nowshed Zamil, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner at the very outset submits that the auction so far held by the court was in violation of Rule 69 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure which provides that where a suit is adjourned under Sub-Rule 1 of Rule 69 for a longer period than 30 (thirty) days a fresh proclamation under Rule 67 shall be made unless the judgment debtor concern to waive it. But in the instant case there was no such waiver of the judgment debtor and, as such, the court ought to have published proclamation a fresh for holding auction. He further submits that for non-compliance of the procedure as contained in Rule 69 the entire auction process has become irregular and questionable. Mr Zamil further argued that non-compliance of the provisions as contained in Rule 69(2), the petitioner has sustained substantial injury by reason of such irregularity. As such, the auction is liable to be set aside. 

 11. Mr. Imam Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the decree-holder opposite party submits that the property in question was placed on auction thrice but no bidder found. Subsequently, the decree-holder purchased the property against its due claim through court with expressed permission not by any auction. As such, a fresh proclamation under Rule 69 is not at all required to publish. It is also argued that an application under Rule 19 of Order XXI is maintainable where any fraud has been practiced in conducting auction sale but in the present case there is no allegation of fraud and the irregularity so have been raised on the part of the petitioner is not at all true. Moreover, he submits that proviso to Rule 19 provides that no sale shall be set aside on the ground of irregularity where the applicant has not sustained substantial injury. 

 12. In the instant case the applicant could not substantiate, by any means, what injury they have sustained. But it is established that even after publishing auction notice they did not come forward to pay the dues and also they utterly failed to make payment of the installments directed by the High Court Division in appeal preferred by them. Therefore, the decree-older had no other option but to purchase the property against their due claim. Accordingly, with the permission of the court the decree-holder purchased • the property and got delivery of possession. After purchase the opposite party decree-holder again sold the property in auction to the opposite party No. 5 being found highest bidder and delivered possession of the same to her. As such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 14. Admittedly, the petitioner along with two others mortgaged the property in question to House Building Finance Corporation ("HBFC") as security against loan. They failed to make repayment of the said loan as per terms and conditions of the sanction. HBFC instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 181 of 1997 before the District Judge, Khulna for recovery of the said loan. The said case was decreed against the petitioner judgment debtor who preferred appeal before the High Court Division which was ended with a direction to the judgment-debtor to pay the decretal amount by installments. But the judgment-debtor failed to pay the decretal amount to the decree-holder. The decree-holder opposite party then put the said decree in execution by filing Execution Case No. 28 of 2003. In the said case the property in question was placed on auction for three times but no bidder was found. Resultantly, the decree-holder opposite party filed an application before the court seeking permission to purchase the property against their dues under Rule 72 of Order XXI. The court allowed the application and sold the property to the decree-holder against their dues and delivered possession. Thereafter, the decree-holder opposite party again sold the property by auction to opposite party No. 5 and delivered possession of the same. 

 15. From perusal of order sheet (Annexure-'C' series to the supplementary affidavit) it is found that the court permitted the decree-holder to purchase the property by its order dated 28-7-2005. Sale certificate was issued on 15-1-2006 and possession delivered to the decree-holder on 13-4-2006. Finally, the case was disposed of vide order dated 25-4-2006. After disposal of the execution case on satisfaction the judgment debtor petitioner came before the court with this application after near about 3 (three) years. Any application under Order XXI, rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure has to be filed within 30 (thirty) days from the date of auction under Article 166 of the Limitation Act. And, as such, the case is therefore, barred by limitation. 

 16. I have gone through the order sheet of the execution case and it has been found that the executing court properly complied with all provisions of Order XXI in disposing mortgaged property in favour of decree-holder. The property in question was not sold in auction but the decree-holder purchased the property with the permission of the court against their claim. Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that a fresh proclamation was not published is not correct. From the papers available in record, this Court finds that no irregularity or fraud has been done in the execution process and disposal of the property in favour of the decree-holder.
